title: South Crete Highlights
tagline: Spili's lion fountains, the Kourtaliotiko Gorge, Preveli Monastery and the palm-forest lagoon in one unhurried day.
seoTitle: Preveli Palm Beach & Monastery Tour from Rethymno
seoDescription: A five-hour private day trip from Rethymno to Spili village, the Kourtaliotiko Gorge, Preveli Monastery and the Preveli palm forest. Photoshoot included.
summary: South Crete Highlights is a five-hour private day trip from Rethymno along the south coast of Crete, run daily for groups of up to eight with hotel pick-up at 09:00. The route starts in the mountain village of Spili and its Venetian lion-head fountains, drops south through the Kourtaliotiko Gorge to the cliff-top Preveli Monastery, and finishes in the Preveli palm forest where the Megalopotamos River meets the Libyan Sea. Difficulty is easy, a professional photoshoot and edited digital album are included, and the price is €200 for a group of up to four.
overview:
South Crete is the unspoiled side of the island, where the mountains run straight down to the sea. The landscape changes constantly along this coast: gorges, rivers, palm groves and quiet beaches that sit well away from the crowds, with small villages scattered across the hills between stone houses, narrow lanes and olive terraces.

Life here is slow. You pass locals going about their day, children playing in the streets and fishermen working along the shore. The air smells of salt, herbs and flowers, and the only soundtrack is waves and birdsong.

This day is built for that pace. You wander, look, swim, eat local food and take your time. It is less a checklist of sights than a chance to feel how the island actually lives, and it works just as well for families as it does for couples.
highlights: The 25 Venetian lion-head fountains in the square at Spili, running with fresh mountain spring water
The stone houses, narrow lanes and unhurried character of a working Cretan mountain village
The towering limestone cliffs of the Kourtaliotiko Gorge, with a stop at a scenic viewpoint
Sweeping views of the Libyan Sea from cliff-top Preveli Monastery, and its role in Crete's resistance under Ottoman rule and in the Second World War
The monastery's quiet courtyard, Byzantine architecture and frescoes
A walk through the grove of rare Phoenix theophrasti palms, native to Crete
The lagoon where the Megalopotamos River meets the sea, calm enough to swim in fresh water
A professional photoshoot along the way, delivered as an edited digital album within 48 hours

itinerary.heading: Spili village
itinerary.body: The day starts in Spili, one of the most charming and authentic mountain villages in southern Crete. Traditional architecture, narrow streets and a slow pace make it a good introduction to the side of the island the resorts never show you. The central square is the reason everyone stops: a row of Venetian lion-head fountains, 25 stone spouts running with fresh spring water off the mountains above. There is time for a short walk through the village, photographs and a coffee before we carry on south.

itinerary.heading: Kourtaliotiko Gorge
itinerary.body: From Spili the road drops south through the Kourtaliotiko Gorge, one of the most spectacular landscapes in southern Crete. It runs between towering limestone cliffs and dramatic rock formations, with the mountains opening up on either side. We make a short stop at a scenic viewpoint to take in the gorge and take photographs. The gorge is known for the strong winds that funnel through it and for the thick vegetation along the river, a green contrast to the bare rock above.

itinerary.heading: Preveli Monastery
itinerary.body: Next is Preveli Monastery, set high on the cliffs above the Libyan Sea. Its long history is closely tied to the history of Crete itself, particularly through the periods of resistance and conflict. There is time to walk the grounds, look at the Byzantine and traditional Cretan architecture and the frescoes, and sit in the quiet courtyard with one of the best sea views on this coast. You will also hear what the monastery and its monks did for the local population under Ottoman rule and again in the Second World War.

itinerary.heading: Preveli Palm Forest
itinerary.body: The last stop is the Preveli palm forest, a natural oasis where the Megalopotamos River reaches the Libyan Sea. It is one of the few places where the rare Phoenix theophrasti, the Cretan date palm, grows in the wild, which makes the grove an ecological rarity as much as a beauty spot. There is time to explore the palm grove, walk along the river, listen to the birdlife and take photographs, and — depending on the season and the weather — to cool off in the lagoon where the fresh water meets the sea. River, palms, mountains and sea in one place is a fitting end to a day on the south coast.

faqs.a: Yes, we stop at the historic Preveli Monastery on the way down to the palm forest. The views of the Libyan Sea from the cliffs there are incredible, and the history is even better.

faqs.q: Is this tour okay for kids?
faqs.a: It is perfect for families. Between the palm forest, the waterfalls and the beach, there is always something new to see. It is a fun, active day without being exhausting.

faqs.q: Can we swim in the river?
faqs.a: Definitely. You can walk through the palm forest and then dive into the fresh river water. It is one of the most unique feelings in Crete.
No, comfortable sneakers or good walking sandals are fine. There is a bit of a descent to get to the beach, but nothing too technical.

Full refund on cancellations made up to 48 hours before the tour.
